en: The carabao, or water buffalo, is the national animal of the Philippines, known for helping farmers plow rice fields.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Philippine government has three co-equal branches: the Executive led by the President, the Legislative, and the Judiciary.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine, is the national flower of the Philippines and is often woven into leis.
The Igorot people of the Cordillera mountains built the famous Banaue Rice Terraces by carving steps into the steep mountainsides.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman accepted to Harvard Medical School and founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines.
Filipino, which is primarily based on Tagalog, is the national language of the Philippines and is written in the Latin alphabet.
The Philippines celebrates Independence Day every June 12 to commemorate Emilio Aguinaldo's 1898 proclamation of freedom from Spanish colonial rule.
The Philippine eagle, characterized by its shaggy crest, is the national bird and one of the largest eagles in the world.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a traditional two-steps-forward, one-step-backward dance performed in the streets.
The South Sea pearl, produced by the Pinctada maxima oyster found in Philippine waters, is the official national gem of the Philippines.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is traditionally demonstrated when community members work together to physically relocate a nipa hut to a new site.
